production_scope: Native landscape candidates only; portraits paused. All ten canonical stanza captions map to source images; 011–012 remain unmapped extras.

continuity.narrative_arc: Roaring clouds terrify Vraja; Krishna reassures the cowherds, uproots and raises Govardhana, keeps the people and cattle sheltered through Indra's seven-day storm, then lowers the hill as the weather clears and the devas praise him.
continuity.krishna_form_contract: Use art/bible/characters/krishna-vrindavan-youth/character.json for every Vrindavan-period youthful Krishna in this dasakam: serene youth (not infant-like), deep matte blue skin, long dark curly hair, yellow dhoti, muted red-orange shawl, plain smooth unmarked forehead, one simple low gold band with one upright peacock feather, ordinary human proportions with one face, two attached arms and hands, two legs and feet. Do not apply this contract to other Krishna life stages or to scenes without Krishna.
continuity.indra_form_contract: Use art/bible/characters/d063-indra/character.json: one distinct adult Indra with one head and two attached arms, simple crown and restrained cream/ochre/maroon celestial clothing; no peacock feather. Storm actions and fleeing belong only to the stanzas that call for them.
continuity.supporting_cast_contract: Ordinary Vraja people and devas have distinct faces, natural human proportions, two arms and two legs. Nanda is one mature moustached cowherd in simple cream and muted olive/green. Cattle are individually coherent and remain distinct from people. Keep groups small enough to avoid cloned faces and fused bodies.
continuity.palette_arc: Flat opaque matte South Indian temple-mural fields: warm cream, earth ochre, deep maroon, muted olive and deep blue Krishna. Storm indigo may enter the sky, but not dominate the mineral palette. No glossy skin, reflective metallic gold, cinematic light, or outer border.
continuity.reference_policy: Numbered intake photographs and their caption mappings guide story and cast context only; do not copy their composition or finish. D001 references guide rendering only. The copied D062 S001 candidate is provisional Krishna face/clothing continuity context, not an approved master or a source for scene composition.
continuity.unmapped_extras: intake/D063/011.jpg has no photo caption; intake/D063/012.jpg contains devotional song text. Preserve both in intake, but do not assign either to a stanza or use song text as a caption.

must_show: Roaring dense rain clouds gather above Vraja, their deep blue color recalling Krishna's complexion.
A small distinct group of Vraja people below look up with concern as the storm spreads; keep the scene before the hill is lifted.
scene_brief.composition: Use a broad landscape: storm clouds occupy the upper field, with a modest Vraja settlement and a few clearly distinct people below. Krishna may be present among them as the youthful blue cowherd, but no hill-lifting action occurs yet.

stanzas.alt: Roaring storm clouds spread over Vraja and alarm its people.

landscape.composition_override: Compose a full landscape cloudscape over Vraja; keep clouds, faces and figures inside the frame.

stanzas.reference_guidance: Use 001.jpg only for the storm-over-Vraja story cue; use D001 only for matte rendering and the D062 candidate only for provisional Krishna identity.

must_show: Driving rain and hail buffet the cowherds and cattle in Vraja.
The frightened group cries for protection while youthful Krishna calmly reassures them not to fear.
scene_brief.composition: Show Krishna among a small distinct group of cowherds and cattle in heavy rain, speaking with a calm protective gesture. This is the appeal and reassurance before the hill is raised.
scene_brief.tone: Urgency softened by Krishna's calm assurance.

stanzas.alt: Cowherds and cattle plead for protection from hail and heavy rain as Krishna reassures them.

landscape.composition_override: Compose a full landscape with rain moving diagonally across a small group and visible cattle; retain clear faces and hands.

stanzas.reference_guidance: Use 002.jpg for the storm and pleading scene only; the D001 images set rendering, and the D062 candidate is provisional Krishna identity context.

must_show: Smiling youthful Krishna quickly uproots Govardhana from its base with his two strong youthful arms.
A few cowherds witness the first lift; show a clear connected contact between Krishna and the hill.
scene_brief.composition: Make the initial uprooting the focal action: Krishna's hands remain visibly attached and connected to the lifted hill at its base. Keep the hill and Krishna in natural proportion; do not imply a detached floating mountain.

stanzas.alt: Smiling Krishna uproots Govardhana to protect Vraja from Indra's anger.

landscape.composition_override: Compose the hill lift with a clear visible hand-to-hill contact and safe margins around the mountain.
landscape.candidate_status: selected native landscape v005 after one authorized repair; Krishna’s forehead is bare while both hands retain clear connected contact beneath the slightly lifted hill; independent exact-checksum review is recorded; no approval implied

stanzas.reference_guidance: Use 003.jpg for the initial uprooting story only; D001 references govern finish and D062 S001 anchors provisional youthful Krishna identity.

must_show: Krishna holds the lifted hill like an umbrella with the lotus of one hand, with unmistakable contact at the underside.
Cowherds, women, cattle and calves shelter beneath on dry soft sand while rain falls outside.
scene_brief.composition: Use the hill as a broad shelter roof over a compact, distinct community and cattle. Krishna stands on the dry sandy ground; the raised hill remains connected to his single supporting palm.

stanzas.alt: Krishna holds Govardhana overhead as Vraja's people and cattle shelter on dry sand beneath it.

landscape.composition_override: Compose the raised hill across a wide frame; keep the supporting palm visibly connected and sheltering figures distinct.

must_show: Krishna continues holding Govardhana with one raised left palm, its underside visibly supported.
He speaks playfully with nearby cowherd companions while using his free right hand to gently scratch a nearby cow; the sheltered group is content.
scene_brief.composition: Frame a quiet human moment beneath the hill: Krishna's raised left hand contacts the mountain, while the connected right arm gently reaches to one nearby cow. Keep bodies and limbs unambiguous.
scene_brief.tone: Easy companionship and contentment beneath the storm shelter.

must_show: One adult Indra, distinct from Krishna, watches the raised Govardhana and doubts that the young cowherd can sustain it.
Indra sends a severe rainstorm toward Vraja, representing seven days of assault; the hill continues to shelter the people.
scene_brief.composition: Place a single Indra in the clouded sky directing the storm toward a small, clearly sheltered Vraja below. Krishna remains a small blue figure under the hill if visible; Indra is the foreground subject.
scene_brief.tone: Pride and threat, kept within flat mural restraint.

stanzas.alt: Indra dismisses the young Krishna's strength and sends a seven-day storm over Vraja.

must_show: Krishna remains perfectly steady under the raised hill as the rain clouds run out of water.
Wind sweeps the spent clouds away while a single frightened Indra flees in the distance.
scene_brief.composition: Show the storm clearing from one side of the frame, with Krishna and Govardhana still steady; Indra retreats far away as a small but distinct figure. Keep the left palm connected to the hill.
scene_brief.tone: Release after a long storm, with Indra's fear secondary.

stanzas.alt: Krishna stands unmoved beneath Govardhana as wind clears the spent clouds and Indra flees.

landscape.composition_override: Compose the shift from storm to clear sky across the wide frame; maintain clear hill-hand contact.

must_show: The rain has stopped and the cowherds and cattle emerge from beneath the hill.

scene_brief.tone: Relief, joy and reunion after shelter.

must_show: A small group of distinct devas praises youthful Krishna after the Govardhana feat.
A restrained symbolic reference to Varaha carrying the earth recalls the verse's comparison, while the main Krishna remains a single two-armed youthful cowherd.

Preserve Varaha's unmistakable boar head and coherent boar body, and do not infer a second Krishna or copy D012's pose. Do not depict Bhattathiri, who is not in the Sanskrit stanza.
